To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the impact of the different facets of employer image on students’ intention of applying to the company differs between countries and 2) the impact of some aspects of employer image (i.e. task attractiveness, perceived career opportunities and perceived working atmosphere) on students’ intention for applying to the company are similar in all four countries.

(1) employer image is a significant predictor of the intention to apply; (2) the impact of employer image on the intention to apply is moderated by the country context; (3) the impact of some employer image facets varies across countries, while the impact of other employer image facets is stable across different countries.
the impact of employer image on students’ intention varies across countries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how to attract talent in a globalised labour market.
the question how to attract applicants in different countries and regions.
the question how to attract applicants in different countries and regions and how to build a successful employer image in the war for talents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
employer branding is a complex phenomenon, which is influenced by various factors, which in turn are influenced by cultural differences.
there is no universal approach to attract talent, but a global employer positioning is possible.
the impact of employer image on the intention to apply is not universal but depends on the specific facets of employer image and on the national culture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
firms need to adapt their branding strategies to the specific characteristics of the target market.
the attractiveness of a firm as an employer depends on a combination of local and global characteristics.
the employer branding strategy needs to be adjusted to the local market conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
firms need to adapt their employer branding to the local context and that they can benefit from a global approach.

firms can build a global employer positioning by focusing on those aspects of their employer image which are stable across different countries, and by adapting their employer image to the local market in terms of those facets which are culturally specific.
companies should focus on those employer branding facets, which are relevant in all countries, while they should adapt the communication of other facets of employer image to the respective country.
